headline: Florida HOAs worsen housing crisis with foreclosures, liens
summary: HOA Spy data reveals over 10,000 foreclosure suits and 460,000 liens filed by associations against members, impacting housing costs and availability.
details: Homeowner and condominium associations in Florida are reportedly exacerbating the housing crisis by contributing to increased costs, reduced availability, and instability for residents. HOA Spy has indexed over 104,000 Florida associations, with data from official court dockets and county records.

The records show a significant number of legal actions initiated by associations against their own members. This includes over 10,000 foreclosure suits, 460,000 claims of lien, and 277,000 lis pendens filings. These actions can pressure homeowners into selling or facing foreclosure.

While a foreclosure suit is not always a lost home, the pressure from these filings is substantial. The debt can escalate with interest, late charges, collection costs, and attorney's fees, all secured by a lien on the property. In some cases, associations initiate foreclosures more often than banks.

Claims of lien, filed before foreclosure, can also hinder homeowners. Title companies may refuse to close sales, and lenders may deny refinancing when a lien is present. In 2025, there were 7,916 claims of lien filed, an 8% increase from 2020.

Recent legislative changes, like Florida's Senate Bill 4-D, mandate structural inspections and reserves for older condo buildings. While intended for safety, these measures increase costs for owners through higher dues and special assessments, potentially leading to unpaid assessments and subsequent association actions.

The financial burden is evident in rising HOA fees. In August 2024, median monthly HOA fees in Tampa rose 17.2% to $614, and in Orlando, they increased 16.7% to $467, further straining homeowners' budgets.
